name: General Motors

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (General Motors (logo with wordmark, horizontal).svg)

description: GM designs, builds and sells Chevrolet, GMC, Buick and Cadillac trucks, SUVs and cars, mostly through independent authorized dealers who buy at wholesale (3.8 million vehicles in 2025, 87 percent in North America). The money is in full-size pickups and SUVs: GM holds 33.0 percent of US truck sales versus 2.1 percent of US car sales. A second business, GM Financial, lends to GM buyers and dealers and earns interest and lease income; it is 9 percent of revenue and produced $2.8B of pre-tax earnings against $10.5B for North American vehicles. China runs through unconsolidated joint ventures (SGMS, SGMW) whose vehicle sales do not appear in GM revenue. 2025 was hit by tariffs and $9.8B of special items, mainly a $7.9B EV capacity write-down; 2026 EBIT-adjusted guidance was raised from $13-15B to $14-16B by the Q2 10-Q.

gics.note: The Wikipedia list gives only GICS sector and sub-industry; industry group and industry are not in that source and are left null, not filled from memory. SEC SIC code from the EDGAR submissions record: 3711 Motor Vehicles & Passenger Car Bodies.

hq.note: 1240 Woodward Avenue, Detroit, MI 48265 (FY2025 10-K cover); incorporated in Delaware in 2009

employees.note: About 155 thousand worldwide: GMNA 119, GMI 28, GM Financial 9; 88,000 hourly and 68,000 salaried; about 47,000 US hourly employees union-represented (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: GM North America (GMNA) (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: GM sells vehicles at wholesale to independent authorized dealers; revenue follows wholesale volume, mix and price net of dealer, retail and fleet incentives. Profit is concentrated in full-size trucks and SUVs. 2025 absorbed higher tariffs and $7.9B of EV charges (the latter excluded from EBIT-adjusted).
businessLines.description: North American vehicle operations: 3,296K wholesale vehicles in 2025, 86.8% of GM wholesale volume (10-K).

businessLines.name: GM International (GMI) (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Wholesale vehicle sales to distributors and dealers; China profit arrives as equity income from joint ventures, not revenue (the China JVs sold 1,880K vehicles in 2025, not in GM revenue). EBIT-adjusted excluding equity income was $426M.
businessLines.description: Vehicles sold outside North America: 503K wholesale in 2025, 13.2% of GM wholesale volume; China is run through unconsolidated joint ventures SGMS and SGMW (10-K).

businessLines.name: GM Financial (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Earns interest, lease and fee income from customers and dealers against its own borrowing cost and credit losses. About $89.7B of net receivables at 2025-12-31; debt of $46.4B at 2026-06-30 (short-term $19.2B plus long-term $27.3B, computed).
businessLines.description: GM's captive finance company: retail loans and leases to vehicle buyers across the credit spectrum and floorplan and other commercial loans to dealers; North America and South America, plus China through joint ventures (10-K).

businessLines.name: Cruise (autonomous driving)
businessLines.how: No meaningful revenue; a cost centre. Cruise restructuring charges were $223M in 2025 and $1,103M in 2024 (adjustments table).
businessLines.description: GM stopped funding Cruise robotaxi work in December 2024; the technical work is combined with GM's to develop driver assistance and automated driving for personal vehicles.

brands.name: Chevrolet
brands.note: Mainstream trucks, SUVs, crossovers and cars, including EVs such as Equinox EV

brands.name: Buick
brands.note: Also sold by the China joint ventures

brands.name: Baojun and Wuling
brands.note: Sold by the China joint ventures (SGMW sold 1,368K vehicles in 2025; SGMS 512K), not consolidated

brands.name: OnStar / Super Cruise
brands.note: Software-enabled services and subscriptions; revenue not separately reported in the excerpts read

brands.name: US mix
brands.note: 2025 US industry trucks 4,592K, GM 1,517K (33.0%); crossovers 9,320K, GM 1,280K (13.7%); cars 2,719K, GM 57K (2.1%) (10-K)

whatsNext.text: About $4.0B to onshore production at plants in Tennessee, Kansas and Michigan over two years from the 2025 announcement, plus nearly $1.0B for a new V8 engine generation in New York
Additional EV supplier-negotiation charges expected in 2026, described as significantly less than 2025's $7.9B
2026 guidance (Q2 10-Q): net income attributable $8.4-9.8B, EBIT-adjusted $14.0-16.0B, EPS-diluted-adjusted $12.00-14.00
